CITY OF ING LEWOOD
  ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
June 5, 2019 7:00 P.M.
Community Room – First Floor
1 West Manchester Boulevard
----------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

2.  Roll Call.

3.  Communications from staff.

4.  Minutes approval  for  November  7,  2018,  Planning  Commission
  meeting.

5.  Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items. Persons wishing to
  address the Planning Commission on any item on the agenda other
  than a public hearing may do so at this time.

6.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  a. A continued public hearing to consider an application by
  Douglas M. Champion representing East Beach Inglewood, LLC for
  Zone Change No. 2018-001 (ZC-2018-001) to allow a zone change
  of an approximately 67,487 square-foot (1.55 acres) site from
  R-2 (Limited-Multiple family Residential) and M-1 (Light
  Manufacturing) to R-4 (Multiple-family Residential) at 355 La
  Colina Drive and 338 to 358 East Beach Avenue (AIN 4015-017-
  003; 017 and 025). This application has been withdrawn.

  b. A public hearing to consider an application by Nathan Kruger
  for Special Use Permit No. 2017-012 (SP-2017-012) for a Final
  Planned Assembly Development (PAD) to allow a six-story,
  104,930 square-foot, 120-room hotel on a 29,931 square-foot C-
  2A (Airport Commercial)at 11111 South Prairie Avenue.

  1. Preliminary Recommendations:
  a. Preliminary Recommendations: Adopt findings and the
  attached resolution approving SP-2017-012 subject to
  conditions.

  c. A public hearing to consider an application by Shanita
  Nicholas, representing Sip & Sonder, for Special Use Permit No.
  2019-005 (SP-2019-005) to allow an event center with live
  entertainment and the sale of beer and wine for on-site
  consumption within a café on a 3,742 square-foot, H-C (Historic
  Core) zoned property at 108 South Market Street.

  1. Preliminary Recommendations:
  a. Preliminary CEQA Recommendations: Affirm Notice of
  Exemption EA-CE-2018-088
  b. Preliminary Recommendations: Adopt Findings and the
  attached resolution approving SP-2019-008 subject to
  conditions.

  1
 7.  NON PUBLIC HEARINGS

  a. A non-public hearing to consider an application by Terry Dulan,
  representing Dulan’s Soul Food Kitchen, for Design Review 2019-
  005 for proposed exterior modifications to the storefront of an
  existing multi-tenant commercial building on an 8,550 square-
  foot property at 202 E. Manchester Boulevard.

  1. Preliminary Recommendations:
  a. Preliminary CEQA Recommendations: Affirm Notice of
  Exemption EA-CE-2019-043
  b. Preliminary Recommendations: Adopt Findings and the
  attached resolution approving DR-2019-005 subject to
  conditions.

  b. A non-public hearing to consider an application by Roy
  Courtney, representing Inglewood Park Cemetery, for Planning
  Commission Review No. 2019-001 for a proposed 19-foot, 11-inch
  pylon sign at the entrance of an existing cemetery on an S-1
  (Special Cemetery) zoned property at 720 E. Florence Avenue.

  1. Preliminary Recommendations:
  a. Preliminary CEQA Recommendations: Affirm Notice of
  Exemption EA-CE-2019-040
  b. Preliminary Recommendations: Adopt Findings and the
  attached resolution approving PCR-2019-001 subject
  to conditions.

  c. A non-public hearing to consider an application by Nathan
  Kruger, owner, for Planning Commission Review No. 2019-002 to
  approve the Public Art Plan for installation of onsite artwork
  related to construction of a new 6-story, 104,930 sf, 120 room
  hotel on a C-2 (General Commercial) zoned property at 11111 S.
  Prairie Avenue.

  1. Preliminary Recommendations:
  a. Preliminary Recommendations: Adopt Findings and the
  attached resolution approving DR-2019-002 subject to
  conditions.

8.  Planning Commission discussion on meeting logistics.

9.  Commission Initiatives

10.  Public Comments. Anyone wishing to address the Planning
  Commission on any matter within their jurisdiction and not
  elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.

11.  Adjournment.

If you will require special accommodations, due to a disability,
please contact the Planning Division at (310) 412-5230 or FAX (310)

Inglewood, CA 90301. All requests for special accommodations must be
received 48 hours prior to the day of the hearing(s).

minutes_text:
MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, JUNE 5, 2019

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, June 5, 2019, in the Community
Room, on the first floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Commissioner Rice, the meeting was called to order
at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Commissioner Erick Holly
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide Trejo
  Commissioner Terry Coleman
  Chairman Larry Springs

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Fred Jackson, Senior Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner
  Taylor Kay, Assistant Planner
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., Director of E.C.D.
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Wilcox stated that application for Item 6a has been withdrawn
by the applicant from further consideration. Item 6b has received
correspondence prior to this evening’s meeting and copies have
been distributed to the Planning Commission and copies have been
made and placed on the sign-in table for the public and suggested
the Commission to take a brief recess to read it, along with the
public. Also a revised resolution has been modified and is
available for the public as well as for the planning commission,
which has been placed at each of the planning commissioners’
chairs.

Chairman Springs made the announcement that there would be a 5-10
minute recess to allow for the reading of the newly received
correspondence by both the planning commission and the public at
this time, which is now 7:20pm.

Ms. Wilcox made another announcement that the copies for the public
and the planning commission have not been printed as of yet, but
will be done within the hour, and will notify the public and the
planning commission when they are ready for reading. In the interim
it was suggested that the planning commission could hear Item 6C
now.

At this time Chairman Springs stated that a motion should be made
to move Item 6B after Item 6C, which will give planning staff
opportunity to have the copies made.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
June 5, 2019

MOTION:

Commissioner Rice made the motion to move Item 6C forward and hear
Item 6B after, and was seconded by Commissioner Holly.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioners Holly, Rice, Trejo, Coleman and Chairman
  Springs.

(4) MINUTES APPROVAL:

Commissioner Holly made the motion to approve the minutes of
November 7, 2018 and was seconded by Commissioner Coleman, and
Abstained by Commissioner Trejo, due to being absent.

MOTION:

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioners Holly, Rice, Coleman and Chairman Springs.

Abstained:  Commissioner Trejo.

(5) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None.

(6) PUBLIC HEARING:

6A. ZONE CHANGE NO. 2018-001(ZC-2018-001) AT 355 LA COLINA DRIVE
AND 338 – 358 EAST BEACH AVENUE. A public hearing to consider an
application by Douglas M. Champion representing East Beach
Inglewood, LLC for Zone Change No. 2018-001 (ZC-2018-001) to allow
a zone change of an approximately 67,487 square-foot (1.55 acres)
site from R-2 (Limited-Multiple family Residential) and M-1 (Light
Manufacturing) to R-4 (Multiple-family Residential) at 355 La
Colina Drive and 338 to 358 East Beach Avenue (AIN 4015-017-003;
017 and 025). This application has been withdrawn.

6C. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-005 (SP-2019-005) AT 108 SOUTH
MARKET STREET. A public hearing to consider an application by
Shanita Nicholas, representing Sip & Sonder, for Special Use Permit
No. 2019-005 (SP-2019-005) to allow an event center with live
entertainment and the sale of beer and wine for on-site consumption
within a café on a 3,742 square-foot, H-C (Historic Core) zoned
property at 108 South Market Street.
Ms.  Marissa  Fewell,  Assistant  Planner,  made  the  staff
presentation.

Chairman Larry Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were
any questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff:
 ABC Licensing has a census-tract that states there is an over-
  concentration of facilities with liquor licenses in the area
  and could staff repeat it for clarification.
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes - that ABC Licensing stated that in the
  area after two like businesses wanting to have Beer & Wine
  Licenses would constitute as over-concentration.
 Then is it true that in the area already there are nine (9) such
  active licenses?
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes – that eight (8) of the nine (9) are
  sit-down restaurants.

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
June 5, 2019

  There was one (1) crime at the subject site, what type and when
  and was the site vacant?
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes, in 2017 per information from Inglewood
  Police Department (IPD), burglary at that address.
  -
Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 Per the IPD stating that there was one crime incident in 2017,
  and none in 2016 or in 2018, was Sip and Sonder operating at
  the time of the burglary? And if not, what type of business was
  operating?
  - Ms. Fewell stated Sip and Sonder was not operating at the
  time, but another establishment was present, a food market
  was occupying the location and there was no sale of beer
  and/or wine at that time.
 Since the property at the subjects location is a multi-tenant
  building, once they obtain a license from ABC, should the
  applicant be approved by this planning commission, will the
  future new tenants have to follow the rules and agreement
  ordered by ABC?
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes, and it will be recorded with the County
  of Los Angeles, enforced and will have to be followed by all
  tenants.
 With regards to special events at the site, will the applicant
  have to go before the permits and licensing board in order to
  be approved for every event or will it be one blanket approval?
  - Ms. Fewell stated that it is a blanket approval.
 Per the staff report, it states for the special events that are
  to be held, “…a small number of attendees will be present”, but
  “a small number” is not truly defining as to the number of
  attendees, and so before giving a blanket approval for special
  events, I would like to have a better definition as to the
  number of expected attendees.
  - Ms. Fewell stated that the applicant is present this evening
  and would be better able to speak to this question.

Commissioner Coleman commented to staff –
 Regarding the adding of one more security camera – to capture
  the front of the establishment and also the addition of staff,
  especially for special events, it increases safety for all.

  All other questions will be for the applicant.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward and address
the planning commission.

Both Ms. Amanda Jane Thomas and Ms. Shanita Nicholas, co-owners of
Sip and Sonder Restaurant addressed the planning commission.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for questions to the applicants
by the planning commission.

Commissioner Holly asked –
 For the applicants to speak to the planning commission as to
  how the community has come out to embrace the business since
  its initial opening and how there has been an increase in revenue
  as well as community participation.
  - Ms. Nicholas stated that it has been an increase that far
  exceeded her expectations in a very short amount of time. The
  fact that a great deal of the community loves the idea that
  there is a great space they can just walk to meet friends for
  anytime of the day and not only customers from within the
  immediate area have been coming during the day/lunchtime, but
  in the early and also late evenings to meet and greet with

  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
June 5, 2019
  old and new friends, co-workers and possible clients. The
  repeat customer fan base has truly been enjoyable to see how
  often they will come if to just be by themselves and sit and
  enjoy not only the atmosphere, but just a cup of tea or
  coffee.
  - Ms. Nicholas stated that several of the new clients have now
  designated Sip and Sonder as a safe meeting space for their
  gatherings which ends up being an all-day session, one in
  particular, the Women’s Writing Group from USC. This is more
  than just a coffee shop, it is being utilized as a “space”
  where many things can take place. There are some that come
  because they need a mid-space to meet between distances from
  Long Beach and Downtown L.A., and so they utilize the space
  here. Also this is a space where customers can take and make
  phone calls to complete various projects.
  Other than having an open space where different people can come
  for coffee, or recordings or other types of programs, are there
  projects or events for the community that only you offer?
  - Ms. Thomas stated that both she and Ms. Nicholas are Attorneys
  at Law, and this requires them to conduct a higher standard
  of diversity and inclusiveness of all members of society. She
  stated that they do operate and are lead for a non-profit
  organization that meets at Sip and Sonder. The L.A. Black
  Investors Club non-profit assists with various Women
  organizations and many groups by offering self-motivating
  talks and sessions, also various communities are impacted by
  this non-profit. One of the members of the L.A. Black
  Investors Club gives talks on starting small businesses,
  which helps many to see the possibilities available to them.
  Along with the recordings and videos made, the space offers
  a great atmosphere for more than just coffee lovers.

Commissioner Rice stated:
 He was able to visit Sip and Sonder recently, and found it to
  be a very pleasant place and wanted to say thank you for bringing
  this project to Inglewood and welcome.
 He stated that various businesses here in Inglewood make sure
  they’re customers have food present along with the selling of
  Beer and Wine, and wanted the applicants to inform the planning
  commission on the various food choices that will be and are
  being sold now at Sip and Sonder and what benefits to both Sip
  and Sonder and the community will take affect with the selling
  of Beer and Wine?
  - Ms. Nicholas stated currently in our coffee shop there are
  sweet and savory snacks, pastries and small food items, pre-
  packaged sandwiches that are available for purchase, and
  since at present there is not a full working kitchen these
  current food items pair very well with our coffees, juices
  and teas. With the various current events that will be taking
  place such as our open mic and spoken word evenings, and when
  the Beer and Wine approval happens, our arrangement is to
  partner with several food delivering services as well as
  connect with some of the local full kitchens near, so that
  there will be the same food continuity with the Beer and Wine
  that is here now with the coffees and teas.
  - Ms. Thomas stated that they guarantee to continue having this
  outsourced feature with bigger and better selections, as it
  is important that their customers will be serviced fully with
  healthy food options.

Commissioner Trejo asked:
 Are there events happening at the Sip and Sonder now?
  - Ms. Nicholas stated that there just the past month, there was
  a small “Open Mic” night, as there happened to be around 15
  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
June 5, 2019
  to 20 people who extended their stay from the late afternoon
  arrival and so with that size in attendance, and it ended at
  10:30pm which extended the operating hours.
  Where did the patrons park during the extended hours for the
  Open Mic night?
  - Ms. Nicholas stated that the parking structure around the
  corner on Locust is open and operating, along with the patrons
  that stayed from the afternoon who parked on the street and
  those that arrived after 6:00pm.
  What do you feel makes Sip and Sonder a unique business model
  and  therefore  provides  for  public  convenience?  Public
  Convenience has to be made because there is an over-
  concentration of liquor licenses. Please describe your business
  model.
  - Ms. Nicholas stated that as it was eluded to earlier that the
  community has come out and supported this business because
  this is the type of place they have been looking for where
  they can come, greet and meet not only old friends but new
  friends, in a space that will allow them the opportunity to
  be free to enjoy their day and evening at a nice pace, where
  they can literally just sit, sip, and sonder the day’s events.
  It is an environment where the community has spoken to how
  they thoroughly enjoy being able to come into Sip and Sonder
  and just relish in the way they are pampered and served. We
  are confident that this environment will continue to grow.

Commissioner Trejo made a statement and then asked:
 At her daily job, her co-workers know that she lives in
  Inglewood, and several weeks prior to the Planning Commission
  they asked where in Inglewood are the new places to eat and just
  enjoy themselves, so she looked up “new places in Inglewood”
  and found Sip and Sonder. She looked at the website and read
  the manifest and found that only a certain demographic was being
  targeted, the website appears to be non-inclusive of all of the
  different cultures that live in Inglewood and feels the answer
  needs to be heard and asked Ms. Nicholas and Ms. Thomas to
  explain why they appear to be targeting just one group of
  people?.
  - Ms. Thomas stated that although it may feel that Sip and
  Sonder’s website is only targeting the African American
  community, we targeted this culture because there are not
  many if any of these types of culture driven places where
  people of color could come and enjoy their heritage proudly.
  Although there are many cultures represented in the City of
  Inglewood and our website does speak to the African American
  community, it’s for that very reason that it speaks to all
  diversities and is very inclusive of all. This was part of a
  review that was posted on “YELP”, within the first weeks of
  opening and it feels very true to me still to this day.

  -  Ms. Nicholas stated that within any organization and business
  that has a goal or mission of some sort, there is a base
  target that matters to the business and what in particular
  they are aligned with, mainly it’s the audience that becomes
  the mission of the business to try to aim for and reach. Sip
  and Sonder is definitely for the community and the culture
  that is Inglewood. The response and statements that we have
  received from those in the community who continue to come
  back to Sip and Sonder speak to the diversity and feel of a
  place that is inclusive for all. This is a great feeling that
  should be continued and celebrated.
  -  Ms. Nicholas stated that with the diverse staff and members
  of Sip and Sonder, it is a “space” that takes on the persona

  5
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
June 5, 2019
  of those that work there - in that space - and the pride that
  they have in serving the clientele, both repeat and new.

Commissioner Trejo asked one more question about
 What does small number represent and especially for the 2:00am
  events, as one person’s version of small may be fifteen, others
  may see small as two.
  - Ms. Thomas stated that the initial desire for the use of the
  space was to not limit the length of a performance, thus
  allowing it to continue until completion. The time of day was
  just a number given, but not intended to always end at that
  time.
  - Ms. Nicholas stated the times listed were what they were
  receiving from the community. If there was a plan to stay
  open late in the evening, Ms. Nicholas stated they would close
  early around 2:00pm and then open back up in the early evening
  such as 6:00pm until around the conclusion of an evening’s
  performance. She stated that the customers requested that if
  Sip and Sonder would be closed on certain afternoons, if it
  were possible to post when Sip and Sonder would be closed in
  advanced and when it would be open and to pick particular
  days and evenings for these performances and so in order to
  not limit the closing time that particular time was chosen in
  order to ensure all performances would have the adequate time
  needed.

Commissioner Trejo stated:
 One important fact that will be reinforced and that is the
  serving of beer or wine must be accompanied with food. There
  are the dangers of one glass of wine and one glass of beer
  leading to two and to have people full of alcohol and nothing
  for them to eat can’t be allowed. So if this SUP gets approved
  that will be a definite condition that will be voted into
  approval.

Commissioner Coleman thanked the audience and the applicant for
staying during this evenings proceedings, along with their
patience and asked the applicant:
 Since their opening in January, how has the attendance from the
  public been up until this point?
  - Ms. Thomas stated that in looking at the numbers the other
  day, there has been a 300% increase in attendance since their
  opening in January. And the growth continues to get larger
  based on pure revenue sales as well as the number of people
  who are inhabiting the space.

Commissioner Coleman asked:
 If you are denied this beer and wine approval, will that put
  your business in jeopardy of closing or will you maintain what
  you presently doing?
  - Ms. Thomas stated that it is a part of our business plan to
  have beer and wine as a staple in order to move forward, we
  have been able to be a successful business thus far, but in
  trying to keep up with the going prices in the area, we will
  need to keep up with our presentation on the street, it will
  be difficult.
 It was mentioned earlier that with large events, having only
  two employees on staff seems very overwhelming, how do you plan
  on handling such a large group with only two people, will you
  hire extra for the event?
  - Ms. Nicholas stated that the general two employees that are
  in the shop during regular business hours usually consist of
  eight employees all together, mainly being two for just the

  6
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
June 5, 2019
  coffee house, but for special events we do have a coordinator
  who will bring on extra staff just for the evening’s event.
  Are you saying that for all special events Sip and Sonder will
  have extra employees on hand for all those events?
  - Ms. Nicholas stated that not necessarily every event, it would
  depend upon the scope and nature of the event and the
  coordinator would determine the need, if for no other reason
  than for the relief of the daily staff and definitely for the
  security of both the patrons and staff.
  - Ms. Thomas also stated that she and Ms. Nicholas also rate as
  staff.
  Currently there are only seven security cameras on the facility,
  and in wanting to secure health and safety to all, there will
  be a need for more security cameras around the facility
  especially two more in the front door area, are you willing to
  add them?
  - Ms. Thomas stated that if this will be a requirement they
  will definitely abide by it, not a problem.

Chairman Springs asked if there was anyone For or Against the
project to come forward.

FOR: / AGAINST:

Lee Johnson, Investment Firm Owner / Sip & Sonder Patron
- For

Lynette Coste, Event’s Professional Entrepreneur / Sip & Sonder
Patron
- For

Courtney Wilkins, Inglewood Resident / Sip & Sonder Patron
- For

Stuart Bailey, Inglewood Resident
- Just a concerned citizen due to the over-saturation
- There needs to be an increase in security cameras (two in the
  rear and one more in the front) and personnel, more staff on
  hand
- For

Chairman Springs asked for closing comments and also a motion from
the Planning Commission.

Commissioner Rice wanted to thank Sip and Sonder and every business
person who has started a business here in Inglewood, and who are
looking to open a business here in Inglewood. This community is a
beautiful melting pot of diversity, and togetherness and for all
businesses to not be afraid to come to Inglewood and open up here.
There should be no fear of going into a business establishment
here, all should feel welcomed and should and will be able to enjoy
one’s self. So, thank you once again Sip and Sonder, and
congratulations.

Commissioner Coleman forgot to ask on large functions will there
be live security guards – will they be armed or not? Staff replied
that the applicant has proposed that on large events there will be
live security guards present, but there was no mention as to if
they would be armed or not.

Ms. Wilcox stated that if the live security officers are armed,
they will go through the appropriate Permits and Licensing
procedures.

  7
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
June 5, 2019

MOTION:

Commissioner Rice made the motion to affirm the categorical
exemption EA-CE-2019-062 and adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2019-005, subject to 17 conditions, add a one year
review of the ABC License for Sip and Sonder and was second by
Commissioner Holly, Resolution No. 1836,
Chairman Springs asked for questions from Planning Commission.

Commissioner Trejo – has additions to the motion and awaits the
appropriate time to add them.

Commissioner Coleman – regarding condition no. seven, if there is
the possibility to add another additional security camera to the
present seven cameras that the applicant stated they are willing
to do.

Chairman Springs asked Commissioner Rice if he is willing to accept
the adding of additional cameras to condition no. seven?

Commissioner Rice asked if he could verify with staff the actual
number of security cameras on the premises at present? Staff
replied that there are no security cameras in the front and only
on security camera in the rear parking lot, so Commissioner Rice
rejects the additional condition proposed by Commissioner Coleman
and submits a new motion.

MOTION:

Commissioner Rice made the new motion to affirm the categorical
exemption EA-CE-2019-062 and adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2019-005, subject to 18 conditions, add a one year
review of the ABC License for Sip and Sonder along with two
additional cameras in the front and two cameras in the rear and
was second by Commissioner Holly, Resolution No. 1836,

Commissioner Trejo wants to make two additional conditions to the
present motion – Condition No. 19, to insist that patrons who order
either beer or wine, must also order food at the same time; the
intent is to ensure that the establishment continues to be a full
service restaurant and not just a beer and wine distributor.

Chairman Springs stated that this will need to be examined further.

Ms. Wilcox asked to make a statement –
1. The one year review of the beer and wine license for the
  applicant is fine as long as it is one year after the receipt
  of the beer and wine license from ABC; and
2. With regards to food – under previous applications the
  condition was that food be available for purchase with the
  alcohol.

Commissioner Trejo stated that to her recollection there was an
establishment on Arbor Vitae years ago who wanted to apply for
beer and wine license and the condition for approval of the beer
and wine license was to insure that food had to be ordered with
the beer and or wine order.

Assistant Attorney Lewis stated that he is not comfortable with
this condition being proposed, where there can be no demand upon
patrons to purchase food. He stated that the planning commission
can require that food sales are available for purchase, but if
there is a strong concern about the sale of beer and wine, then
  8
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
June 5, 2019
possibly deny the application for the license to ensure no beer
and wine sales without food.

Commissioner Trejo stated that she feels this is a wonderful
establishment and does not want to hinder their application for
the beer and wine license, this is just to curb the loitering that
takes place on Market Street and the over saturation of beer and
wine locations.

Chairman Springs stated that to resolve this issue, he will return
to Commissioner Rice to see if he will accept this added condition
to his motion?

Commissioner Rice stated that the only condition he will accept is
that a strong and present food source be made available for
purchase by the patrons of the restaurant, and Commissioner Trejo
stated that she would accept this version of the condition.

Commissioner Trejo stated that she has a final condition and wants
it labeled condition no. 20 for the motion – which has to do with
events ending after midnight shall only occur three times per
month.

Chairman Springs asked Commissioner Rice if he will accept this
condition, Commissioner Rice stated yes; then Chairman Springs
asked Commissioner Holly since he seconded the initial motion,
will he accept this 20th condition, after deliberation he stated
yes.

That resolution no. 1836;

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
